candidate.statement: let sha = await run(`git rev-parse ${tag}`, { cwd: repoDir });
candidate.selection_reason: user-controlled tag directly interpolated into git rev-parse command -> executed via shell -> potential command injection
candidate.source_summary: The tag parameter is passed directly from the caller (gitDiffApply function) which receives it as a function argument. The tags (startTag, endTag) come from user input to the gitDiffApply module's exported function.
candidate.sink_summary: The tag is directly interpolated into a shell command `git rev-parse ${tag}` which is executed via child_process.exec() in the run function. The exec() function uses shell execution by default.
candidate.guard_summary: No validation, sanitization, or escaping of the tag parameter before interpolation into the shell command. The tag is used as-is in backtick string interpolation.
candidate.risk_pattern: User-controlled input (tag parameter) is directly interpolated into a shell command string without validation or escaping, then executed via child_process.exec() which spawns a shell.
used_variable_sources: tag parameter from checkOutTag function call
called_function_context: run() from ./run module which uses child_process.exec()
enclosing_conditions: No conditional guards around the command execution
candidate.context_summary: The checkOutTag function is called multiple times in index.js with startTag and endTag parameters that originate from user input to the gitDiffApply module. The tags are used to check out specific git tags by executing git commands.
